subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should this issue be fixed as a narrow stale literal-OpenAI auto route/doctor owner repair, folded into the broader shared session-state resolver in #87957, or treated as expected for explicit `/model openai` sessions with better diagnostics?
rationale: Current source shows DeepSeek is not directly claimed by Codex, but persisted OpenAI selection becomes authoritative and Codex doctor ownership still omits literal `openai`; the reporter also clarified an explicit `/model openai` action, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Repair stale OpenAI route drift first
options.body: Fix auto-sourced `openai` session pins and doctor ownership for non-OpenAI primaries while preserving user-sourced OpenAI selections.

options.title: Fold into shared resolver
options.body: Make #87957 the canonical owner and add this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload scenario to its acceptance criteria before closing this issue later.

options.title: Treat explicit OpenAI selection as expected
options.body: Keep OpenAI-to-Codex behavior for user-pinned OpenAI sessions and improve `/status` or doctor messaging to make the state clear.

recommendation.title: Repair stale OpenAI route drift first
recommendation.body: Fix auto-sourced `openai` session pins and doctor ownership for non-OpenAI primaries while preserving user-sourced OpenAI selections.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex runtime boundaries, and the session/status surfaces implicated by the decision.
